security_audit.summary: Most alerts match video terminology, translated prompts, or normal text formatting. The review confirmed Windows execution-policy bypass, unsafe recursive cleanup, and missing resource limits for rendering and image decoding. No evidence of credential access, unauthorized data transfer, or prompt injection was found in the reviewed material.

remediation.issue: Windows composition bypasses PowerShell execution policy.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the bypass and use a trusted PowerShell executable that respects the user's configured policy. Report composition failures clearly.

remediation.issue: Renderer cleanup can delete existing staging data.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique staging directory for each render. Remove only directories created by that run and never recursively delete a caller-supplied directory.

remediation.issue: Episode specifications can cause unbounded rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Validate finite durations and cap the shot count, total runtime, frame count, and audio allocation before starting render workers.

remediation.issue: Thumbnail audit does not limit PNG decoding.
remediation.suggestion: Limit file size, dimensions, and decoded bytes before allocating pixel buffers. Reject malformed images with an individual audit warning.

content.value_statement: Blocky characters can change shape, faces, or outfits between generated shots. Define a consistent cast, plan timed scenes, and check for visual drift before production.
actual_capabilities: Create avatar cards with fixed palettes, block proportions, face decals, and signature gestures.
Plan timed vertical storyboards with a clear reaction, camera move, and sound cue for each shot.
Compile English and Chinese first-frame and motion prompts with model-specific camera wording.
Check prompts for inconsistent limbs, realistic faces, crowded shots, and unclear gaze targets.
Render local avatar crops and preview frames, then compose boards and MP4 or GIF animatics on Windows.
limitations: Final board and video export uses Windows PowerShell, System.Drawing, and FFmpeg. Node.js alone does not produce the finished video.
The skill writes prompts for external video models but does not submit jobs to them.
Drift checks are heuristic and do not guarantee consistency in generated footage.
The local renderer uses supported sets, props, and poses rather than importing Roblox Studio projects.

use_cases.title: Plan a vertical comedy short
use_cases.description: Break a short story into timed beats, with one clear action and one camera move per shot.

use_cases.title: Define a recurring cast
use_cases.description: Create avatar reference cards with stable silhouettes, face decals, color palettes, and signature reactions.

use_cases.title: Review shots before editing
use_cases.description: Check prompts and local keyframes for inconsistent hands, blocked sightlines, and hard-to-read speech bubbles.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Draft an avatar card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a classic R6 avatar for [character concept]. Give me its palette, face decal, fixed body proportions, and front, three-quarter, and side reference prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Plan four shots
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a short premise into a timed storyboard.
prompt_templates.prompt: Storyboard a 15-second vertical short about [premise]. Use four shots with one action and one camera move each. Include a visual payoff and short speech bubbles.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Repair visual drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [shot prompt] for [video model]. Correct the blocky hands, face, and joint motion without changing the scene. Return a revised prompt and first-frame anchor.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compile a shot pack
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a multi-character episode for image-to-video generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [episode specification] to compile English and Chinese prompts for [video model]. Preserve each cast member's look, gaze target, and prop contact. Include framing and drift checks.

output_examples.input: Plan a 15-second vertical coffee shop short where an overfilled mug surprises a blocky chef.
output: 0 to 3 seconds: Close on the rising foam as the chef stares at the cup.
3 to 7 seconds: Pull back as the chef stops pouring.
7 to 11 seconds: Hold a medium shot as the foam settles.
11 to 15 seconds: Show a tiny foam peak landing on the chef's hat. Add a light pop.

output_examples.input: Fix a shot where a classic R6 avatar grows fingers while lifting a mug.
output: First-frame anchor: Show the mug flush against the flat end of the avatar's solid block hand.
Motion: Lift the arm at the shoulder hinge while preserving the hand shape and flat face decal.
Remove references to gripping fingers, wrist bends, and rounded human palms.

best_practices: Use the same palette, face decal, and outfit details in every shot.
Use a first-frame reference when continuity matters across clips.
Use trusted input files and a fresh output folder for local rendering.
anti_patterns: Put several primary actions into one short generation clip.
Use finger-grip descriptions when the avatar has solid block hands.
Treat external prompts or a passing drift check as a finished video.

faq.question: Can I create a storyboard without rendering or using an external model?
faq.answer: Yes. You can request a text storyboard, an avatar card, or a video prompt pack without an external account.

faq.question: What do I need for local MP4 or GIF export?
faq.answer: The bundled workflow uses Node.js, Windows PowerShell, System.Drawing, and FFmpeg. Rendering and video assembly do not require an online account.

faq.question: Does the skill generate clips on an external video platform?
faq.answer: No. It prepares prompts for tools such as Kling, Seedance, Hailuo, Wan, Sora, and Runway. Submit them separately.

faq.question: Which avatar styles are available?
faq.answer: The skill describes classic R6, segmented R15, and chibi blocky styles. The local preview renderer uses its built-in character geometry and poses.

faq.question: Can the drift checker inspect a finished clip automatically?
faq.answer: The checker reads prompts, shot specifications, and optional PNG thumbnails. Review finished clips separately for motion and continuity.

faq.question: Is this an official Roblox tool?
faq.answer: No. It is an independent skill for a blocky visual style. It does not publish to Roblox or replace Roblox Studio.
